_what_this_is: CARRIED ITEMS AND STANDING RULINGS THAT BELONG TO NO ONE FORM'S MAP. Every map carries its own `_carried` list and every form's gate reports that list's length, which works exactly as long as the item belongs to a form that HAS a map. A ruling made about 433-D before 433-D has a map has nowhere to live, and a ruling with nowhere to live is a ruling that evaporates - which is the failure this construct exists to prevent, one level up from the per-map lists.
_the_rule: Unresolved is fine. Evaporating is not. An item leaves this file in exactly two ways: it is RESOLVED, with what resolved it, or it is WITHDRAWN, with why it was not a question after all.
_how_an_item_leaves_for_a_map: When the form it names gets a map, the item is COPIED into that map's `_carried.open` in the first commit of that form's track and marked `migrated_to` here. It is not deleted: a cross-form ruling that shaped a form's first prompt should still be readable from outside that form.

open.subject: 433-D's duplicate pages need a declared `mirror`, and a mirror is a declaration and not an exemption
open.the_shape: Page 3 of 433-D is the taxpayer's copy of page 1. Every leaf stem appears exactly TWICE across the two pages, and the same value must reach both copies.
open.why_it_is_a_problem_today: That is INTENTIONAL double-binding, and the duplicate-write guard has correctly forbidden double-binding since Prompt 4. A map that binds one key to two targets is the exact shape of the defect that guard exists to catch, so 433-D cannot be mapped under the current rules without either breaking the guard or declaring the mirror.
open.the_ruling: Declare it. A `mirror` block names the mirrored pairs, and the declaration is CHECKED: every stem in a mirrored pair appears exactly twice, both copies receive the same value, and a stem bound to only one copy is a STOP. An exemption would be a hiding place - it would let any second binding through under the word 'mirror'. A checked declaration is not.
open.built_when: 433-D's FIRST prompt, not before. Recorded here so the ruling survives the seven or more prompts between the two OIC forms and 433-D.

open.subject: 433-H is out of this engine's scope, and the revision pin cannot mean there what it means everywhere else

open.subject: exclusionSites() still attributes a method call to a same-file predicate; the exposure is now measured, the mechanism is not fixed
open.the_mechanism: CALL is /\b([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/g and \b matches after a ".", so `someMap.norm(...)` in an exclusion position is attributed to a same-file `const norm`. Reachability killed the cross-file case; this is what is left.
open.what_is_different_now: The exposure is a DERIVED 0 rather than an observation, re-derived on every validate-map run and every sweeps run by adapters/pdf/enumerate-shadowing.mjs, with a canary that fires every verdict and an unreadable row treated as a STOP. The day the number stops being 0 is a reported finding with the file, the line, the predicate and its defining module named.
open.what_would_close_it: Read the character before the identifier inside exclusionSites() and refuse a site where it is a ".". That is a change to the function every entry in PREDICATES is measured by, so its no-op path has to be proved across all twenty-eight entries and every site they cover in the same run — the standard the reachability change was held to. The enumerator above is what that proof would be run against: it already names, per site, whether the attribution rests on a bare call.

open.raised_in: Prompt 46 commit 1, by guard-sweep.mjs on the first run after rx() adoption
open.subject: A probe string that QUOTES CODE reads as a code site to every sweep that scans source, and each one has to be disposed by hand
open.the_shape: rx() registrations state the strings a regex must match and must not match, and for a regex that reads source those strings ARE source: `matches: ['s.matchAll(re)', 'new RegExp(x)', 's.match(re)']` in blanket-audit.mjs was read by guard-sweep's [extract] selector as an extraction site with no disposition. One phantom on this cycle, disposed as [G-149]. Every future probe that quotes code lands the same way, in whichever sweep's selector its text happens to satisfy.
open.why_it_is_not_settled_here: The two obvious remedies are both worse than the symptom. Teaching every source-scanning sweep to skip lines inside an rx() spec is a change to four selectors at once, and a selector taught to ignore a region is a selector that can be made to ignore a real site by moving it there. Assembling probe strings from fragments so they do not look like code makes the probe unreadable, and an unreadable probe is one nobody checks against the regex it is meant to prove. Neither is worth doing on one instance.
open.the_measurement_that_would_settle_it: How many phantoms adoption produces per registered regex. Twenty-four registrations produced one. If that ratio holds, hand disposition is cheaper than any mechanism; if a later cycle adopts widely and the count rises, the shape of the fix is a shared "this is data, not code" marker that every source scanner in the engine reads from one place, rather than four independent skip rules.
open.reported_where: guard-sweep.mjs [G-149] disposes the one live instance and says in its `why` that it is a probe string rather than an extraction.

open.form: engine-wide; the instance is on 433-A, the form gen-fields-from-map.mjs writes
open.subject: gen-fields-from-map.mjs’s lineRef regex has NO backstop, and guard-sweep [G-94] claimed one that does not exist
open.the_shape: [G-94] disposed of `const m = /^(S?\d+[a-z]?)_/i.exec(key);` as sound, ending: "A dead regex would make EVERY key report null, and that is caught one level out: adapters/hubspot/validate-crosswalk.mjs compares the generated file against the crosswalk, whose bindings carry the printed markers independently." VALIDATE-CROSSWALK.MJS DOES NOT READ line_ref ON ANY FORM. It opens crosswalk.<form>.json, the map and the backbone field file, and joins them by `key` and `hs_name`; the string "line_ref" does not occur in it. It reads fields.433a.json only as the BACKBONE, by hs_name and key. And until [D-16] it could not be run on 433-A at all — the form gen-fields-from-map.mjs actually writes — because 433-A has no crosswalk: it is the backbone.
open.how_it_hid: Nobody had run the named backstop against the named claim. This is the same shape as [S-21], where count-sweep disposed of 269 claim sites in asset-row-shapes.json on this same file’s coverage of an artefact it had never opened, and [R-13] is the rule both earned. A forward reference launders an intention into a fact, and the more precisely it is worded the more readers it convinces.
open.what_is_actually_true: The site’s OWN reasoning stands and is unchanged: lineRef returning null writes `line_ref: null` into the output rather than dropping the field, so a no-match is a recorded answer a reviewer sees, and no empty input makes the site report success. What does not stand is the downstream catch. adapters/pdf/regex-self-assert.mjs leaves this file unadopted under a stated ground — "a wrong verdict changes a generated property type, which assert-intake-keys.mjs and generator-guard.mjs compare against the form engine on every run" — and that ground covers this file’s TYPE regexes. line_ref is a display column and no downstream check reads it, so the stated ground does not reach it.
open.why_it_is_not_settled_here: The remedy is either to adopt this regex into regex-self-assert.mjs with probes, which is a change to a registered set that five forms load, or to decide that a display-only column needs no backstop and say so in the boundary register as an exclusion with its reason. Both are rulings and neither is this prompt’s scope, which is [D-16] and 433-B page 4. [G-94] has been corrected to state what is true and to cite this id instead of a check that does not exist — the correction is landed; the backstop is not.

resolved.subject: count-sweep.mjs MANIFEST has no duplicate-id check, and a collision merges two dispositions silently

resolved.raised_in: Prompt 40, commit 3 - found by the exclusion sweep on the first run after a new file was added
resolved.subject: exclusion-sweep.mjs builds its predicate universe from NAMES, so a local const in any swept file makes every same-named call anywhere in the engine an exclusion site - including calls to built-in methods
resolved.the_mechanism: enginePredicates() collects every `const|let|function NAME = (` across the swept files into one flat set of STRINGS. exclusionSites() then scans every exclusion position - `if (X) continue`, `.filter(f => ...)` and three more shapes - and attributes the site to any called name that is in that set. Neither step asks WHERE the name was defined, whether the call is in the same file, or whether the callee is a bare identifier or a method on an object.
what_it_did_twice: FIRST, SILENTLY, FOR THREE SLICES. Register entry [X-16] disposed of `if (!field.isChecked()) continue;` in adapters/pdf/verify-appearances.mjs. isChecked is PDFCheckBox.prototype.isChecked, a pdf-lib method, and pdf-lib is not swept. It was in the universe only because adapters/pdf/run-form-gate.mjs happened to declare an unrelated local `const isChecked = (target) =>` inside gate step 11. Hoisting that local for [B9] turned it into an object property, the name left the universe, and the orphan check finally named the entry. The entry was RETIRED in commit 1 of this prompt with its text kept verbatim.

THEN IMMEDIATELY, LOUDLY, IN THE OTHER DIRECTION. adapters/pdf/assert-completeness-counters.mjs was added in commit 3 with a local `const get = (id) =>`. On the next run the sweep reported UNREGISTERED for `catOf.get(b.entry) !== 'new'` at adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs:200 - a call to Map.prototype.get, in a file with no connection to the new one. One new local in one file made a built-in method call in another file an unregistered exclusion and took the gate down.
resolved.why_the_second_direction_is_the_useful_o: The first direction hides a real site behind a false disposition and nothing complains. The second is a STOP and complains immediately. So the failure mode that matters is the FIRST: any register entry in PREDICATES may be disposing of a call that is only in scope by accident, and the way to find out is not to wait for the accident to end.
resolved.the_fix_is_not_here: Distinguishing a bare call from a method call means reading `X.name(` differently from `name(`, which is a change to exclusionSites() - the function every entry in PREDICATES is measured by - and its no-op path would have to be proved across all 25 registered entries and every site they cover in the same run. That is a change to a guard and not slice work.
resolved.what_slice_2_did_instead: Renamed the local to counterFor, which removes the collision without touching the sweep, and recorded the mechanism here. The rename is a workaround and is named as one: the next file to declare a `const get`, `const has` or `const find` will do the same thing again.
resolved.resolved_in: Prompt 41, commit 1 — exclusion-sweep.mjs predicates keyed on their defining module
resolved.what_it_got_right: The mechanism, exactly as written. enginePredicates() did collect every definition across the swept files into one flat set of STRINGS, exclusionSites() did attribute a site to any called name in that set, and neither step asked where the name was defined or whether the calling file could reach it. Both directions described here reproduced on demand.
resolved.what_it_got_wrong: One sentence: "the fix is not here … distinguishing a bare call from a method call means reading `X.name(` differently from `name(`". That is ONE possible fix and it is not the one the defect needed. REACHABILITY kills both accidents on its own and never has to look at the call syntax: isChecked is neither defined in nor imported into verify-appearances.mjs, and `get` is neither defined in nor imported into reclassify-against-backbone.mjs, so both sites leave the universe without any judgement about what a dot means. The bare-versus-method question is a separate and smaller exposure, and it is now [D-09] rather than a blocker on this one.
resolved.how_it_was_closed: predicateDefinitions() returns name -> the set of swept files defining it; reachableIn(file) returns the names that file can actually reach, from its own definitions and from the named imports it declares, each resolved back to the module that defines it. An exclusion site carries `definedIn`. Every PREDICATES entry names its defining module (one, or a list where the same one-line predicate is genuinely declared in several files), and sitesFor() matches on the pair. The orphan check, the completeness check and [EX-90] all moved to the pair.
resolved.proved_by: runReachCanary(), a three-file synthetic tree held in memory: x/a.mjs defines a predicate, x/b.mjs calls a same-named METHOD and imports nothing, x/c.mjs imports the predicate from x/a.mjs and calls it. The rule must attribute NOTHING to x/b.mjs and exactly one reachable name to x/c.mjs, RESOLVED BACK TO x/a.mjs. Both directions are asserted, because a rule that attributed nothing to anybody would pass the first half alone. Printed on every run of the sweep.
resolved.what_it_cost_to_find: The rescoping found a live instance on its first run: `covered` is defined in blanket-audit.mjs and, this commit, also in the new sweep-boundary.mjs. Under the old rule [EX-20] — a disposition written about a forward-reference filter — would have silently absorbed a gitignore test in an unrelated file. It is now [EX-29], with its own reason.

resolved.raised_in: Prompt 41, commit 1 — split off [D-08] when reachability closed the half that mattered
resolved.subject: exclusion-sweep.mjs still does not distinguish a bare call from a method call, so `x.norm(...)` matches a `norm` defined in the SAME file
resolved.the_mechanism: CALL is /\b([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/g over the text of an exclusion position, which matches the identifier before a "(" whether or not a "." precedes it. Reachability now requires the name to be defined in or imported into the calling file, so the cross-file accident is gone. What survives is the same-file case: a file that defines `const norm = ...` and elsewhere calls `someMap.norm(...)` in an exclusion position attributes that site to its own predicate.
resolved.why_it_is_smaller_than_D_08: The dangerous direction of [D-08] was a register entry standing over a call the file could not even see — a disposition sound only while a name collision held, in a file nobody would think to check. This one is confined to a single file, where the definition and the call are both in front of whoever reads the disposition, and the entry names the file. It can still be wrong; it can no longer be wrong invisibly.
resolved.what_would_close_it: Read the character before the identifier and refuse a site where it is a ".". That is a change to exclusionSites(), which every entry in PREDICATES is measured by, so its no-op path has to be proved across all twenty-eight entries and every site they cover in the same run — the same standard the reachability change was held to, and the reason it is not being done in the same commit as slice work.
resolved.the_current_exposure: Zero sites in this tree are known to be in this state. That is an observation and not a proof: nothing enumerates it, which is itself part of what would close this.

Closing the mechanism is a change to the function every one of the twenty-eight register entries is measured by, and its no-op path has to be proved across all of them in the same run — carried on as [D-10] so the remaining work is not read as done.

resolved.raised_in: Prompt 43 commit 1, by the 433-B(OIC) declaration-coverage union
resolved.subject: a declared printed constant of ZERO can never be reported as exercised, because the coverage test is `constant !== 0`
resolved.the_shape: run-form-gate.mjs step 11 records a declared constant as `{ constant, fired: konst !== 0 }`. Every printed constant in this repo so far is the SAME one — "if the vehicle is leased, enter 0 as the total value", drawn on the page in words — and its value is 0. So `fired` is false on every record that takes the leased branch, INCLUDING the records that take it correctly and print the 0 the caption instructs. Five instances are live: 433-A(OIC) `6a leased` and `6c leased`, and 433-B(OIC) `4a leased`, `4b leased` and `4c leased`.
resolved.why_it_is_a_problem_today: The coverage union names all five as "in class somewhere and proved nowhere", beside floors and predicates that genuinely have never been driven. Those are different facts. A reader closing gaps works down that list and cannot close these, and a list with permanently uncloseable rows on it stops being a list anyone works down.
resolved.what_it_is_NOT: It is NOT a defect in the forms and NOT a gap in the fixtures. samples/433boi.overmax.sample.json parks two vehicles on `lease` and samples/433boi.slice3.sample.json parks a third there; all three branches HELD, the constant WAS applied, and the printed cell carries the 0 the caption asks for. The gate proves the branch. What it cannot report is the application of a value whose contribution is indistinguishable from not applying it.
resolved.the_candidate_ruling: `fired` for a constant should mean THE BRANCH THAT CARRIES IT WAS TAKEN AND THE CONSTANT WAS ADDED, not `the constant moved the sum`. That is a change to a guard's own coverage rule, so it needs its own commit, its own canary, and a re-read of every other `fired` predicate in that table for the same conflation — `factor` has it too (`fired: cellSum !== 0` cannot distinguish a factor applied to zero from a factor not applied) and `sign` has it (`fired: cellSum !== 0`).
resolved.why_it_is_not_fixed_here: A refactor of a guard is a change to the guard. Prompt 43 §4 asks for 433-B(OIC) fixtures, crosswalk, provisioning and round trip; rewriting the coverage predicate for three declaration kinds across four forms mid-provisioning is exactly the kind of adjacent change that has twice now reproduced the defect class it was meant to close. Recorded with its instances counted so it cannot evaporate.

_resolution.ruling: THE CANDIDATE RULING, TAKEN. `fired` for a constant, a factor and a sign now means THE BRANCH THAT CARRIES IT WAS TAKEN AND THE DECLARATION WAS APPLIED — not "the declaration moved the sum".
_resolution.why_reaching_the_line_is_the_proof: The three pushes sit after the feeder's `when` predicate has held (or declared none), after every target has resolved through the map, and after every cell has been read off the filled PDF and parsed as money. Any of those failing breaks out before the push. So `fired: true` is true BECAUSE of what the code above it did, rather than being written true.
_resolution.all_three_kinds: constant, factor and sign were all `<the sum moved>`. All three are corrected in one edit, because the conflation is one conflation and fixing the constant alone would have left the same sentence meaning two things in the same table.
_resolution.nothing_was_lost: The old predicate said something real: a .8 applied only to zero cells has never been proved to be .8 rather than .7 — the shape of the 0.7 quick-sale cell in the name-lie registry. That fact is KEPT under the name it actually has. Each entry now carries `observable` beside `fired`, the gate reports the applied-but-unobservable set with its identities, and declaration-coverage.mjs unions those identities across a form's fixtures exactly as it unions coverage.
_resolution.and_what_the_fix_would_have_lost_if_it_h: With `fired` = applied, a factor, constant or sign can no longer appear in the coverage residue at all — and a residue a kind cannot enter is a residue that has stopped watching it. Two lists were added in the same commit to take that over: APPLIED-BUT-NOT-OBSERVABLE, and DECLARED-BUT-NEVER-IN-CLASS — a declaration the totals file declares that no fixture in the set ever reached. The second is derived from the totals file, which is the DECLARING artefact, because the runs cannot report a declaration none of them saw.
_resolution.what_moved: Reported in full in the run: five zero constants across two forms left the "in class somewhere and proved nowhere" list, which is what made that list uncloseable, and reappeared in the observability list where they CAN be closed by a fixture that parks a non-zero figure on the leased branch.
_resolution.the_defect_this_fix_committed_and_the_sw: The DECLARED-BUT-NEVER-IN-CLASS check builds a declaration identity from the totals file and compares it against the identities the gate builds. Its first draft formatted the constant with `toFixed(2)` where the gate uses a grouping formatter — agreeing on 0.00 and disagreeing on every figure above a thousand — and reported three real 433-A(OIC) constants (-1,000.00, -3,450.00, -11,980.00) as reached by no fixture when all three are reached on every run. A re-implementation of an identity is a second answer to the question the identity exists to make one answer to, committed by the tool reporting on that class. The formatter now lives once, in adapters/pdf/comparisons.mjs, and both sides import it.

resolved.raised_in: Prompt 47 commit 1, by adapters/pdf/assert-examined.mjs on its first complete run
resolved.subject: adapters/hubspot/validate-crosswalk.mjs THROWS on every form whose crosswalk was DERIVED rather than hand-authored, so it has never examined one row on 433-A(OIC) or 433-B(OIC)
resolved.the_shape: Two crosswalk shapes exist in this tree and the validator was written for one of them. The HAND-AUTHORED shape (crosswalk.433f.json, 97 bindings; crosswalk.433b.json, 0) carries `hs_name` and `classification` on every row. The DERIVED shape, written by adapters/hubspot/derive-names-433aoi.mjs and derive-names-433boi.mjs (239 and 113 bindings), carries `entry`, `fact`, `type`, `fieldType`, `type_basis` and `pii`, and NO `hs_name` at all — the name is derived downstream and lives in the naming-derivation report. validate-crosswalk.mjs line 100 reads `r.hs_name.toLowerCase()` unguarded, so `node adapters/hubspot/validate-crosswalk.mjs 433aoi` and `... 433boi` both die with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toLowerCase)` before printing anything.
resolved.how_it_hid: NOTHING RAN IT ON THOSE FORMS. npm run crosswalk:433boi calls derive-names-433boi.mjs, reclassify-against-backbone.mjs and assert-intake-keys.mjs — not this validator. It is invoked by hand, per form, and it had only ever been invoked on the form it was written for. A guard nobody points at a form is indistinguishable from a guard that passes on it, and that indistinguishability is exactly what [R-04] and adapters/pdf/assert-examined.mjs exist to end: the matrix reported the pair as NOT REPORTED, which is a louder state than a zero, and this is what was behind it.
resolved.what_it_does_NOT_mean: It is NOT a hole in the 433-A(OIC) or 433-B(OIC) crosswalks. Both are covered by other guards that DO run on them and DO report non-zero examined counts: adapters/hubspot/assert-intake-keys.mjs (101 and 65 option values plus row shapes) and adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs, plus the naming-derivation reports and their dry-run and read-back records. What is missing is THIS validator’s four assertions — every engine input bound, no key or name used twice, names legal and permanent before they exist, and the prefix matching the classification — on the derived path.
resolved.why_it_is_not_fixed_here: A REFACTOR OF A GUARD IS A CHANGE TO THE GUARD. Teaching validate-crosswalk.mjs the derived shape means deciding what its four assertions MEAN when the name it checks does not exist in the artefact it is reading — the name is derived, so either the validator derives it (a second implementation of the derivation, which is the shape [D-11] committed and its own sweep caught) or it reads the naming-derivation report (a second artefact, with its own staleness). That is a decision, it needs its own commit and its own regression across both forms, and Prompt 47’s scope line is the standing rules, the examined counts, the overflow log and 433-B pages 2 and 3. Recorded with its instances counted so it cannot evaporate.
the_two_options: THE VALIDATOR READS THE NAMING-DERIVATION REPORT. It keeps its four assertions verbatim and takes `hs_name` from the report the derive-names tool wrote, which is the artefact that actually holds the name. Cost: a second artefact in the loop, and a report that is stale relative to the crosswalk would be validated instead of the crosswalk.

THE VALIDATOR SPLITS BY SHAPE AND ASSERTS WHAT EACH SHAPE CAN CARRY. On the derived path it drops the three name assertions and keeps the two that do not need a name — every engine input bound, no key used twice — and SAYS SO in its report, with an examined count per assertion rather than one for the form. Strictly less checking than the hand-authored path gets, and honest about which half it is doing.
resolved.what_is_true_under_both: The pair is REPORTED by adapters/pdf/assert-examined.mjs on every run rather than left as a silence, and it is reported as a DECLARED GAP citing this id rather than as a bare absence — so the day the validator is taught the derived shape, the declaration stops matching and the register says so.

_resolution.ruling: THE VALIDATOR SPLITS BY SHAPE AND ASSERTS WHAT EACH SHAPE CAN CARRY — the second of the two options this item recorded. The shape is detected FROM THE ROWS, never from a list of form names, because a per-form list would assert only that no other form had worn this shape yet, which is [R-06]’s prefix defect in a new place. A crosswalk mixing the two shapes is a STOP: a partial name column is the one state under which "no name used twice" checks a subset and reports a pass.
_resolution.what_it_now_examines_per_form: Every form, and the counts are the guard’s own EXAMINED lines rather than this entry’s assertion: 433f 534 items over 8 assertions, 0 declared gaps. 433aoi 835 over 5, 4 declared gaps. 433boi 341 over 5, 4 declared gaps. 433b 88 problems over 8 assertions on a crosswalk that is empty by declaration. 433a NOT APPLICABLE, and that is derived from the backbone PATH rather than typed as a form name, so the two cannot drift into naming different forms.
_resolution.the_third_form_this_item_did_not_know_ab: THIS ITEM SAID "live on 433-A(OIC) and 433-B(OIC) today". IT WAS THREE FORMS, NOT TWO. On 433-A the validator died with a raw ENOENT stack — there is no crosswalk.433a.json and there never will be, because 433-A IS the backbone every other form is read against. The item counted the forms that threw a TypeError and missed the one that threw an ENOENT, which is the same defect class the item is about: a form nobody had pointed the guard at.
what_the_fix_found_that_had_gone_uncaugh: THE ENGINE-INPUT KEY SPACE WAS WRONG ON 433-B. Groups were read as `d.array || d.source`, and all eight of 433-B’s groups declare neither — fill-433b.mjs reads `input(g)`, the group NAME. All eight collapsed to a single `undefined`, so the guard reported eight real engine inputs as missing and one input that does not exist as present. It said so out loud on every run as "MISSING binding for engine input: undefined" and nothing else contradicted it, because the crosswalk it was checking against is empty.

A FIFTH ENGINE-INPUT BLOCK WAS MISSING ENTIRELY. `check_here` — a lone box with no counterpart cell — is read by fill-433aoi.mjs:195 and fill-433boi.mjs:186, and declares 17 keys on 433-A(OIC) and 10 on 433-B(OIC). The other three forms declare none, which is exactly why its absence was invisible on the one form this guard used to run on. The two engines FILTER it differently (fill-433aoi.mjs requires a string `target`; fill-433boi.mjs skips the `_` prefix) so the key space takes the INTERSECTION, which is the only set both engines agree they read.

TWO 433-A(OIC) ROWS CITE A `backbone_key` THAT IS NOT IN THE BACKBONE FILE. s4_business_name cites 433f_biz_name and 40_monthly_rent_payment cites 433f_exp_rent; neither is in fields.433a.json and both are in fields.433f.json. They are not broken — they are deliberate rebinds onto properties 433-F created, and the second IS the monthly-rent rebind [R-06] cites as its own precedent. A guard reading one field file cannot see a rebind [R-06] licenses.
_resolution.how_backbone_key_now_resolves: THE BACKBONE WINS, AND THE OTHER FIELD FILES ARE CONSULTED ONLY FOR WHAT IT DOES NOT HOLD. That ordering is load-bearing, not a convenience. Five logical keys — bank_accounts, investment_accounts, digital_assets, vehicles, business_income_expense_route — exist in more than one provisioned field file under DIFFERENT hs_names, because they are the same words about DIFFERENT LEGAL PERSONS, which is the subject axis [R-06] exists to name. Four of the five are cited as a backbone_key today, by 433-F and 433-A(OIC), and every one of those citations means 433-A’s. Letting the backbone settle any key it holds makes all four unambiguous by construction. A key the backbone does NOT hold, appearing in two other field files under two names, is a STOP rather than a first match; nothing cites such a key today, and the check is there so the day one does it is not resolved by directory order.
_resolution.what_this_item_got_WRONG: Two things. (1) The form count, above — three, not two. (2) "It is NOT a hole in the 433-A(OIC) or 433-B(OIC) crosswalks." That was TRUE of the crosswalks and FALSE of the key space they are checked against: the missing `check_here` block meant 27 real engine inputs across the two forms were outside the universe this guard compares bindings to, and the first run that could see them reported all 27 as EXTRA bindings not consumed by the engine. Nothing was wrong with the crosswalks; the guard’s idea of what the engine reads was short by a whole block, and no run had ever been able to say so.
_resolution.what_this_item_got_right: The mechanism, the cause and the remedy. The two shapes are exactly as described, the TypeError is at the line named, the reason nothing ran it is the reason given, and the option it labelled second is the one taken. Its instruction that the declaration must stop matching the day the validator is taught the derived shape is what forced adapters/pdf/assert-examined.mjs to be edited in the same commit rather than left asserting a gap that had closed.
_resolution.the_four_declarations_that_remain: A4 no hs_name used twice, A5 name legality and prefix, A6 reuse-before-creating by classification, A7 option extensions. All four need a name or a classification the derived artefact does not carry. They are printed on every run with the reason and the tool that covers each instead, and they are COUNTED — 4 on each derived form — rather than skipped. They are no longer cited to this item, which is closed; they are the guard’s own standing declaration about what a derived crosswalk can be asked.
